The Criminal Petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for brevity 'the Cr.P.C.,')/Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for brevity 'the BNSS') seeking to quash proceedings against Petitioners/Accused Nos.4 and 5 in Cr.No.05 of 2026 on the file of Mahila UPS, Nellore, SPSR Nellore District, registered for the alleged offence punishable under Sections 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for brevity, 'the BNS') and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for brevity, 'the D.P.Act').
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
Perused the record.

3. The petitioners, being the in-laws of Respondent No.2, allegedly harassed her over her salary,
interfered in her marital life, and, along with her husband, subjected her to mental harassment.
She therefore returned to her parental home and alleged that the accused abused her family and that her husband consumed alcohol at home in the company of other women.
As seen from the record, the alleged offences levelled against the Petitioners/Accused Nos.4 and 5 are punishable with imprisonment for less than seven (07) years.
Dr. YLR, J Dated 02.03.2026 4.

sentences.text: (iii) After lodging of the complaint or the FIR, no action should take place without concluding the "Cooling-Period" of two months.
During this "Cooling-Period", the matter may be referred to Family Welfare Committee in each districts.

(iv) Every district shall have at least one or more FWC (depending upon the geographical size and population of that district constituted under the District Legal Aid Services Authority) comprising of at least THREE MEMBERS.

Its constitution and function shall be reviewed periodically by the District & Sessions Judge/Principal Judge, Family Court of that District, who shall be the Chairperson or Co-chairperson of that district at Legal Service Authority.
(vi) The member of the FWC shall never be called as a witness.
(vii) Every complaint or application under Section 498A IPC and other allied sections mentioned above, be immediately referred to Family Welfare Committee by the concerned Magistrate.

After receiving the said complaint or FIR, the Committee shall summon the contesting parties along with their four senior elderly persons to have personal interaction and would try to 2022 SCC OnLine All 395 Dr. YLR, J Dated 02.03.2026 settle down the issue/misgivings between them within a period of two months from its lodging.

(viii) The Committee after having proper deliberations, would prepare a vivid report and would refer to the concerned Magistrate/police authorties to whom such complaints are being lodged after expiry of two months by inserting all factual aspects and their opinion in the matter.

On the basis of the interpretation given by us, we conclude as follows:
a. An arrest by a police officer is a mere statutory discretion which facilitates him to conduct proper investigation, in the form of collection of evidence and, therefore,
shall not be termed as mandatory.
b.
Consequently, the police officer shall ask himself the question as to whether an arrest is a necessity or not, before undertaking the said exercise.

c. For effecting an arrest, qua an offence punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years,
the mandate of Section 35(1)(b)(i) of the BNSS, 2023 along with any one of the conditions mentioned in Section 35(1)(b)(ii) of the BNSS, 2023 must be in existence.
d. A notice under Section 35(3) of the BNSS,2023 to an accused or any individual concerned, qua offences punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years, is the rule.

e. Even if the circumstances warranting an arrest of a person are available in terms of the conditions mentioned under Section Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.5191 of 2021, dated 15.01.2026 Dr. YLR, J Dated 02.03.2026 35(1)(b) of the BNSS, 2023, the arrest shall not be undertaken, unless it absolutely warranted.

but he shall follow the procedure prescribed under Sections 41 and 41(A) of 'the Cr.P.C.,' (now Sections 35 and 35(3) of 'the B.N.S.S.,' 2023).
The petitioners are obliged to render their fullest cooperation in the ongoing investigation.

12. In the result, the Criminal Petition is disposed of directing the Investigating Officer to comply with Section 35(3) of 'the BNSS'/41-A of 'the Cr.P.C.,' and to strictly follow the directions issued in the cases of Satender Kumar Antil, Arnesh Kumar and MD. Asfak Alam.
